sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 371 ± 33.6 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Western blot confirmed expression of the HA-tagged GPR19 protein; no functional assay (e.g., signalling, ligand binding) was reported.
sites.rationale: L1/L2/L3 (all PMC10218176) describe a full-length, membrane-anchored human GPR19 construct explicitly described as 'N-terminally tagged'. The topology landmarks place the N-terminus in an extracellular region (residues 1–67) with no signal peptide, so the tag prepends before M1 (insert_after_residue=0). This is the only extracellular terminus of GPR19, making the junction unambiguous by topology derivation. Python confirmed residue 1 = M and sequence length = 415. Full-length human GPR19 with an N-terminal triple-HA (3xHA) tag was transiently transfected into HEK293 cells; the construct was obtained from OriGene and expression was confirmed by Western blot 24 h post-transfection.

sources.claim: The cDNAs for a hemagglutinin (3xHA)-N terminally tagged human GPR19 receptor (obtained from OriGene, Rockwille, MD, USA) and an empty plasmid (pcDNA3.1+: Invitrogen-Life Technologies) were transfected into the cells with Lipofectamine ® 3000, using the manufacturers’ instructions.

literature_notes: L1, L2, and L3 all originate from PMC10218176 and describe the same construct; L1 is cited as the primary supporting line. L4 (PMC4775022) describes a C-terminal FLAG tag on mouse GPR19 cloned into c-Flag pcDNA3; the topology landmarks place the C-terminus (residues 331–415) entirely intracellular, so this is recorded in other_positions only. No ledger line supports an insertion in any of the short extracellular loops (ECL1 123–139, ECL2 202–223, ECL3 298–309) of GPR19, so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: Mouse GPR19 C-terminal FLAG tag (c-Flag pcDNA3 vector); the C-terminus of GPR19 is intracellular (topology: IC4 331–415), so this tag faces the cytoplasm and is not a surface-accessible site.
